title: Robust JSON fuzzing and regression suite for quantized function-calls
creator: Asha Menon
description: Background: We have observed schema-conformance regressions under some FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles when models produce structured function-call outputs. This ticket establishes a reproducible fuzzing and regression test harness that 1) systematically stresses structured output generation under quantized runtimes, 2) surfaces per-profile failure modes (missing fields, wrong types, extra keys, nesting/array corruption), and 3) provides automated mitigations and CI gating for releases. Goal: deliver a nightly regression suite + a set of actionable mitigations (fallback policies, post-validate heuristics, calibration recommendations) integrated with the evaluation dashboard and a follow-up PR for runtime-1.21.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible fuzzing harness that can run on CI and Dedicated compute and completes within 90 minutes for the core regression set
Baseline dataset (200 seed function-call prompts + 50 curated edge-cases) executed across FP8/INT8/mixed profiles and temperature sweep (0.0, 0.2, 0.8)
Metrics computed: JSON schema pass-rate, field-level precision/recall for required fields, extra-field rate, and mean token delta vs. fp32 baseline
Automated dashboard updates for nightly runs and alerting when schema pass-rate drops > 2% vs baseline
At least two mitigation strategies validated (per-layer fallback and prompt-level post-validate + repair) that recover > 80% of failures for the most common regression class
tasks: Design fuzzing mutation operators for structured outputs (field drop, type flip, array truncation, key reorder)
Implement harness that runs model variants (fp32 baseline, fp8-profile-A, int8-profile-B, mixed) and captures tokens + KV-cache metrics
Create canonical schema corpus: 200 function call prompts + 50 edge-case inputs from customer incident logs
Add CI job (nightly) that runs the core regression set on Dedicated and stores artifacts to s3 and dashboard
Integrate result thresholds into console-2026.03 pipeline (alerting + release block)
Document calibration checklist for quant profiles and recommended fallback policies in Confluence
progress_updates: 2026-02-15: Kickoff meeting with Applied ML and Runtime teams. Agreed core metrics and seed dataset size.
2026-02-22: Initial harness prototype implemented (mutation operators + schema validator). Found early issue: FP8-profile-A shows array-truncation for nested arrays in 4/200 seeds.
2026-03-02: Calibration experiments run on a small sweep (int8-profile-B + bias-correction) — reduced numeric drift but schema pass-rate unchanged for type-flip errors.
2026-03-07: Design decision: add a lightweight post-validate repair step in the SDK as an interim mitigation while we investigate kernel-level fixes. PM approved for release gating.
2026-03-10: Harness integrated with nightly CI runner; first nightly job completed and pushed artifacts to the experiment dashboard.
test_results_summary: Early results: fp8-profile-A baseline run (200 seeds, temp=0.2) produced overall JSON schema pass-rate of 94.5% vs fp32 baseline 98.7%. Failure modes skewed to: (1) missing optional nested arrays (45% of failures), (2) integer->float type flips in small integers (30%), (3) extraneous punctuation leading to parse errors (25%). INT8-profile-B showed 96.2% pass-rate. Mixed precision (fallback on critical layers) recovered average pass-rate to 98.0% but with ~6% latency regression. Post-validate repair recovered ~70% of parseable failures when applied conservatively.
notes: Mutation operators limited to syntactic edits; semantic-preserving mutations planned for next cycle.
Will instrument KV-cache hit/miss traces to correlate cache state with schema failures (early hypothesis: cache eviction + misaligned position encodings amplifies truncation) .
Consider a per-route quantization profile whitelist where critical structured-output routes default to mixed-precision.
